newsitem.title: USA: U.S. stocks post strong midday gains on tame CPI.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stocks post strong midday gains on tame CPI.

text.p: U.S. stocks rallied at midday on Tuesday, cheered by a report showing benign inflation at the retail level and some strong corporate earnings reports.
The Dow shot up 88 points, or 1.4 percent, to 6540. The gains came after blue chips rose 60 points on Monday, their strongest rally in three weeks.
Market players said investors were relieved that the March Consumer Price Index data did not confirm the inflationary pressures suggested in Friday's Producer Price Index report.
The Dow fell 148 points on Friday.
"It's a sigh of relief that our worst fears were not materialized," said John Church, chief investment officer at the Glenmede Trust Co, of the rally on Tuesday.
Analysts had said that an unexpectedly high CPI number would have done major damage to both bonds and stocks.

But the U.S. Labor Department said the CPI rose 0.1 percent in March, after rising 0.3 percent in February. Excluding the volatile food and energy components, the index rose only 0.2 percent after being up the same amount in February.
Economists had expected, on average, the CPI to rise 0.2 percent and 0.3 percent excluding food and energy.
On the back of the inflation news the benchmark 30-year Treasury bond jumped 31/32, its yield falling to 7.09 percent from Monday's close at 7.17 percent.
Analysts said, however, the one piece of data did not signify a clear trend and fears of further Federal Reserve interest rate hikes could quickly resurface.
Solid earnings from banks and other companies including Merrill Lynch and Co Inc and Harley-Davidson Inc also supported stocks.
Merrill Lynch rose 2-7/8 to 90-3/4, Harley-Davidson gained 3-1/8 to 38, and Citicorp, one of the banks reporting first quarter earnings, rose 2-5/8 to 109-1/8.
"The earnings seem to be fine," said Jay Meagrow, a trader at McDonald & Co. "But this time around people are looking at the next quarter, rather than right now."

A prime example of the market's concern over future earnings was semiconductor giant Intel Corp. Intel's shares fell 3-1/2 to 130-1/4 after it reported first-quarter earnings well ahead of Wall Street expectations but warned its second quarter revenues may be flat with the first quarter's.
Intel's decline weighed on other high technology stocks, with Cisco Systems Inc down 2-5/8 to 50-5/8 and Ascend Communications Inc down two to 43-1/2.
The Nasdaq composite was up two points at 1219 but off its morning high of 1229.

"A lot of people are trying to sell into the strength this morning in technology, thinking we're not out off the woods yet for earnings," said Guy Truicko, equity portfolio manager at Unity Management.

Avant! Corp tumbled 11-7/16 to 13-1/16 after the Santa Clara County, Calif., district attorney's office said it filed felony charges against Avant!, its president and other senior officials for allegedly stealing Cadence Design Systems Inc technology.
The two companies make software that helps engineers design computer chips and have been bitter rivals. Cadence Design rose 7/8 to 31-7/8.
